hormuz.label: Middle East war
hormuz.value: Disrupted since Feb 28; October attacks at a war high

facts.text: US and Israeli strikes on Iran on Feb 28 led to the near-closure of the Strait of Hormuz, which normally carries about a fifth of world oil.
Lloyd's List counted at least 28 confirmed attacks around Hormuz in October as of Oct 22, the most in any month since the war began.
Reports on traffic conflict: Lloyd's List saw 'relatively elevated' transits in early October and Trading Economics cites flows near prewar levels, while Reuters on Oct 26 called Hormuz largely shut.
Oct 26: the Houthis said they hit pumping stations on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, an export route around Hormuz. Saudi Arabia did not confirm.

hormuz.say: The root shock is still the Middle East: attacks around Hormuz are at a war high, and the Houthis claim strikes on Saudi export routes.
hormuz.keepReason: Ongoing: October has the most Hormuz attacks of the war, and claimed Houthi strikes on Saudi export routes lifted Brent to a six-month high on Oct 23.

cheapai.label: Cheaper AI models

facts.text: Jul 17: Moonshot's Kimi K3 helped fuel a selloff in tech and chip stocks; traders compared it to the DeepSeek shock of early 2025.
Oct 19: DeepSeek's latest model update pushed a Bloomberg gauge of Asian chipmakers to its lowest since July.
Sep 10: DeepSeek V4.1-Flash claimed much lower memory needs per task.

cheapai.say: Cheaper models keep raising the question of how many chips future AI really needs.

aicapex.label: AI capex boom

facts.text: Meta now guides 2026 capex of $135–145B, mostly for AI infrastructure. Q3 capex was $34.91B.
Meta's free cash flow turned negative (−$2.1B) in Q3, and its shares fell nearly 7% on Oct 22.
Hyperscaler capex plans are expected to keep bond issuance elevated into next year.

aicapex.say: AI capex keeps rising, and at Meta it now exceeds the cash the business generates.

oil.label: Oil

facts.text: Brent settled at $116.72 on Oct 23, a six-month high, up 6.24% on the week. WTI closed at $103.27.
Still below the 2026 intraday peak of $126.41 set on Apr 30.
Brent eased to about $115 on Oct 26 as Saudi Arabia held talks with Iran. It is up about 18% over the past month and 77% over the year.

oil.say: Brent is near $115, a six-month high, but still below the April peak of $126.

inflation.label: Inflation pressure

facts.text: US CPI rose 3.7% over the year to September. Gasoline rose 9.1% in the month, over half of the monthly increase; core rose 0.3%.
University of Michigan year-ahead inflation expectations rose to 4.7% in October, from 4.6% in September.
Canadian CPI rose 3.1% in September, led by gasoline (+27.8%). Excluding gasoline it rose 2.2%.

inflation.say: Oil is pushing headline inflation up on both sides of the border, while core is calmer.

issuance.label: Bond supply
issuance.value: Heavy Treasury and corporate issuance, incl. AI debt

facts.text: Macquarie's Thierry Wizman attributes this year's yield rise more to bond issuance than to inflation.
He expects hyperscaler capex plans to keep issuance elevated into next year.

issuance.say: Part of the yield move is plain supply: more bonds, including AI-related debt, need buyers.

overcap.label: Chip-demand doubt
overcap.value: Market fears AI compute is overbuilt

facts.text: Since July, investors have questioned the assumption that AI compute demand always exceeds supply.
This is the market's interpretation. Neither Meta nor DeepSeek said demand has peaked.

overcap.say: The scarcity story cracked: investors now ask whether chip demand has peaked.

fed.label: Fed
fed.value: 3.75–4.00% after the Sept hike · next decision Oct 28

facts.text: On Sep 16 the Fed raised its target range by a quarter point to 3.75–4.00%, its first hike in more than three years.
Next decision Oct 28. Markets expect a hold; CME FedWatch odds of a December hike are above 80%.

fed.say: The Fed hiked in September and is expected to hold on Oct 28, with a December hike largely priced.

y10.label: US 10-yr yield

facts.text: The 10-year closed at 5.31% on Oct 5, its highest close since May 2002. It started 2026 at 4.19%.
It fell to 4.96% on Oct 22, its first close below 5% since Sep 22, as investors bought Treasuries in the tech selloff. It was 5.00% on Oct 23.
Drivers: inflation, Fed hikes, and heavy bond supply including AI-related borrowing.

y10.say: The 10-year hit 5.31% in early October, its highest since 2002, and is now about 5%.

realy.label: Real yields
realy.value: 10-yr TIPS 2.66% (Oct 23), up from 1.72% before the war

facts.text: The 10-year TIPS yield was 2.66% on Oct 23, up from 1.72% on Feb 27, the day before the war began. It peaked at 2.95% on Oct 5.
So the rate move is not only inflation expectations; real borrowing costs rose too.

realy.say: Real yields are up almost a point since February, so this isn't only an inflation-expectations story.

boc.label: Bank of Canada
boc.value: 2.25% since Oct 29, 2025 · ~81% hike odds for Oct 28

facts.text: The policy rate has been 2.25% since Oct 29, 2025.
Markets price about an 81% chance of a hike to 2.50% on Oct 28, and 19 of 34 economists in a Reuters poll expect one.
Employment fell by 68,000 in September and unemployment rose to 6.5%.
Headline CPI was 3.1% in September, but only 2.2% excluding gasoline.

boc.say: The BoC is in a stagflation bind: 3.1% inflation, falling jobs, and a likely hike on Oct 28.

energy.label: Energy stocks

facts.text: The Energy Select Sector SPDR (XLE) is up 58.14% this year through Oct 23.
At the end of September energy was up 40.28% YTD, with Q3 expected earnings growth of 111.4%.
FactSet: upward revisions to energy EPS estimates were among the largest contributors to the rise in Q3 blended growth since Sep 30; it is now 29.5%.

energy.say: Energy is up nearly 60% this year as oil climbs.

gold.label: Gold

facts.text: Gold was about $4,017 on Oct 26, down 2.4% over the past month. Its record was $5,608 in January 2026.
It hit a three-month low just below $4,000 before recovering on Oct 26, ahead of the Fed decision.
Traders say high oil makes a higher-for-longer Fed more likely, which weighs on non-yielding gold.
Jefferies (Aug): 10-year TIPS yields rising from 1.94% to about 2.41% helped drive gold roughly 25% below its peak.

gold.say: Gold is near $4,000, far below its January record of $5,608, as higher real yields and Fed hike bets raise the cost of holding it.

credit.label: High-yield credit

facts.text: HY spreads rose from 2.66% on Sep 21 to 3.40% on Oct 22, the widest since Mar 30 (3.46%, the 2026 high). They were 3.38% on Oct 23.
CCC-and-lower spreads reached 13.56% on Oct 23, up from 10.75% on Sep 22 and wider than at any time since at least 2023.
CoreWeave's bonds yielded near 15% in mid-October on concern about AI borrowing.

credit.say: Credit is widening fast at the weak end: CCC spreads are the widest in years, and AI borrowers are in focus.

semis.label: Semis & tech
semis.value: Chips' worst day since June on Oct 22 (SOX −6.7%)

facts.text: Oct 22: the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) fell 6.7%, chip stocks' worst day since June 23, as Meta's negative free cash flow revived AI financing worries.
Lam Research also warned that supply constraints for some components will limit chipmakers; its CEO expects the industry to be 'caught up very shortly'.
In September the opposite happened: technology was the only sector that rose.

semis.say: Chips had their worst day since June on Oct 22 as AI financing worries returned.

cad.label: Canadian dollar

facts.text: USD/CAD fell from 1.4273 on Oct 14, its 2026 high, to 1.3993 on Oct 23 (Fed H.10 rates).
Rising expectations of a BoC hike are supporting the loonie.
CAD is also a commodity currency, so high oil helps it.

cad.say: Hike bets and oil have pushed the loonie back below 1.40 per US dollar.

sbcorr.label: Stock–bond corr.

facts.text: Since March, SPY and long Treasuries have mostly fallen together as headline CPI rose from 2.4% to 3.7%. The 60-day correlation reached +0.56 in early June.
Oct 22: SPY fell 1.2% while long Treasuries rose 1.9%. The 20-day SPY–TLT correlation fell to −0.30, its lowest since early March, and ended the week at −0.24.
That day investors 'flocked to the safety of defensive sectors and safe-haven U.S. Treasuries' as the Nasdaq fell 2.6%.
AQR: a positive correlation is a poor reason to swap bonds for more equity risk.

sbcorr.say: Bonds stopped hedging while oil drove inflation, but the hedge came back on the Oct 22 tech selloff.

factor.label: Quality > momentum
factor.value: Q3: value, yield and quality beat momentum

facts.text: In Q3, US value, yield and quality moved ahead of momentum and high-volatility stocks.
Q2 was the exception, when momentum was on top.

factor.say: Quality and value are beating momentum as money gets expensive.

breadth.label: Equal vs cap weight
breadth.value: Tech ~40% of S&P 500; equal weight +3.5% vs −0.4% (1M)

facts.text: Information technology was 39.7% of the S&P 500 in September.
More than half of S&P earnings growth comes from AI infrastructure; semis alone are over 40%.
Over the past month to late October, the equal-weight S&P 500 ETF (RSP) rose 3.5% while the S&P 500 fell 0.4%, on track for its biggest outperformance since April 2009.

breadth.say: Owning the index is a concentrated AI bet: tech is about 40% of it.

edges.why: Lost Gulf supply and tanker risk lift crude.
Fuel and freight costs feed headline inflation and expectations.
Higher realized prices lift producer earnings.
Sticky inflation pushed the Fed into its first hike in over three years.
Gasoline lifted Canadian CPI to 3.1%; the BoC is expected to hike to stop it spreading.
Hike expectations lift the whole curve.
Tightening raises rates after inflation, not only nominal rates.
Hyperscalers borrow to build data centres.
More bonds to absorb pushes yields up.
Higher borrowing costs make the same AI build-out more expensive to fund.
Gold pays no coupon, so higher real yields raise the cost of holding it.
Refinancing gets costlier, and the weakest borrowers feel it first.
Higher discount rates hit long-duration growth valuations.
When inflation drives rates, bonds and stocks fall together.
Low-debt, cash-rich firms hold up when money is expensive.

Doubts about future chip demand hit semis and memory.
Tech weakness drags the cap-weighted index more than equal weight.
Momentum was crowded in AI winners, so its unwind favors quality.
Hike bets support the loonie.

chains.name: Is the bond hedge back?
chains.script: Bonds are starting to hedge again, but only partly. For most of 2026 oil drove inflation: Brent hit a six-month high of $116.72 on Oct 23 after claimed Houthi attacks on Saudi oil sites, and US CPI reached 3.7%. That pushed the Fed into a September hike and the 10-year to 5.31% on Oct 5, so stocks and bonds fell together. When AI-spending worries hit tech on Oct 22, the hedge returned: SPY fell 1.2% while long Treasuries rose 1.9%, and the 20-day correlation dropped to −0.30. While oil drives inflation the hedge stays unreliable, so I'd keep duration moderate and add other diversifiers. Watch the Fed on Oct 28.

chains.name: Why gold falls in a war
chains.script: Gold falling during a war looks odd until you follow the chain. Oil lifts inflation, the Fed tightens, and real yields rise: the 10-year TIPS yield is 2.66%, up from 1.72% the day before the war. Gold pays no coupon, so higher real yields raise the cost of holding it. That's why gold is near $4,000, far below its January record of $5,608. The latest leg is Fed pricing rather than real yields, which eased in October: a December hike is more than 80% priced. Watch the Fed on Oct 28.

chains.name: The AI funding squeeze
chains.script: AI capex and rates are pulling against each other. Hyperscalers are spending and borrowing heavily: Meta guides $135–145B of capex this year, and its Q3 free cash flow turned negative. Bond supply like this is one reason the 10-year hit 5.31% on Oct 5, its highest close since 2002. Higher yields then raise the cost of funding the build-out and lower the value of long-duration growth stocks. Investors are testing that squeeze: Meta's shares fell nearly 7% on Oct 22 when its cash flow turned negative.

chains.name: The AI repricing
chains.script: The AI scarcity story has been cracking since July. Cheaper Chinese models keep raising doubts about how many chips AI really needs, and DeepSeek's latest update pushed a gauge of Asian chipmakers to its lowest since July on Oct 19. Those doubts weigh on chip stocks, and money is moving to the average stock: over the past month the equal-weight S&P 500 rose 3.5% while the S&P 500 fell 0.4%. With tech near 40% of the S&P, owning the index is a concentrated AI bet, which argues for equal weight and for quality over momentum.

chains.name: Oil's winners and Canada's bind
chains.script: Oil cuts both ways for Canada. It lifts energy stocks, with XLE up about 58% this year. But gasoline pushed Canadian inflation to 3.1% in September while jobs are falling, down 68,000. That's a stagflation bind for the Bank of Canada: markets price about an 81% chance of an Oct 28 hike. Hike bets are already supporting the loonie, with USD/CAD back below 1.40. Watch whether the BoC looks through gasoline: inflation excluding it is only 2.2%.

chains.name: Rotation to quality
chains.script: Expensive money is sorting companies by balance sheet. High-yield spreads widened from 2.66% in September to 3.40% on Oct 22, the widest since March. The weak end is worse: CCC spreads reached 13.56%, wider than at any time since at least 2023, and CoreWeave's bonds yielded near 15% in mid-October. Leveraged borrowers feel higher rates first. In equities the same logic shows up as quality and value beating momentum, as they did in Q3. I'd favour strong balance sheets in both credit and equity.
